about: Every catch (\Throwable) under lib/Service that answers null or [] within its first three statements. ServiceCatchReturnsNullTest fails on a site that is not here, on an entry whose site is gone, and when the count passes the ceiling. The ceiling only goes down.

This is a debt list with a ceiling, not an endorsement. The class and the reason on each entry were written by the triage that seeded this file on 2026-09-13 from the site's own evidence: what it returns, and whether and how it logs. They say what the site does, not that the site is right.

The refusal class is deliberately absent: a site where a rule said no is converted to a RefusedException and leaves this file (REQ-QG-CRN-2). Four left it on 2026-09-13, all four in the guard-resolver class hydra gate 8 exists for. Any entry below may turn out to be a refusal when someone reads it; that is what the next batch is for.

The proposal measured 47 sites over a three-LINE window. This instrument counts three STATEMENTS, because a multi-line logger call in front of the return is the same shape and a line window cannot see it. The same tree reads 90 by lines and 203 by statements.

Merging development on 2026-09-14 brought new sites with it, and moved one. #2719 added `Substitution/HumaniqLeaveReader::readLeave#1`. #2732 split `Flow/CaseFlowActions` and added `Flow/PlannedSeriesLedger::optional#1`, `::plannedFlows#1` and `::rowsOf#1`, which is also where `CaseFlowActions::plannedFlows` went, so that entry is removed here rather than kept. The ceiling went 203 to 206 for those four sites and nothing else.

2026-09-14, openspec/changes/one-date-write-path: three nulling date parsers left lib/ (CaseEnricher::normaliseDate, TermijnTimerService::dateOrNull, WorkQueueService::parseDateOnly) and three CaseDateNormaliser sites arrived, two zone-resolution degradations and one read-path reader. The ceiling is unchanged at 206; every write path refuses now instead of answering null.

2026-09-14, openspec/changes/inbound-mail-filters: nine sites arrived with the mail intake path. Eight are degradations of an OPTIONAL app, Nextcloud Mail, which is absent on most instances and whose service, account, attachment, folder and event readers each log at warning and answer the documented empty value; the ninth is the read-miss on an intake log entry. The ceiling went 206 to 215 for those nine and nothing else.

2026-09-14, openspec/changes/case-grants-name-their-source: four sites arrived with OpenRegisterGrantsGateway, the one place dossiq asks OpenRegister who may do what on a case. All four are degradations of an app that may be absent or may predate openregister#3726, and each logs at warning naming what was absent. The null is load-bearing rather than tolerated: the caller reads null as "carry on" and false as "OpenRegister refused", and collapsing the two would lock every handler out of every case on an instance that has not upgraded. The ceiling went 215 to 219 for those four and nothing else.

2026-09-15, openspec/changes/handing-a-case-over: four sites arrived with the internal handover. All four read something and answer the documented empty list when the read cannot be made: three are degradations of OpenRegister being absent or unconfigured and each logs at warning naming what it was reading, and the fourth is a read miss on a case. None is a refusal: every rule this change enforces throws RefusedException and is translated by the controller, which is why the handover's own refusals (an unresolvable team, a settled handover, an unreadable case) are nowhere on this list. The ceiling went 219 to 223 for those four and nothing else.

2026-09-15, openspec/changes/dependent-term-follows-predecessor (REQ-RCL-12/13): three sites arrived with the typed relation labels and the derived sub-case. Two are degradations of OpenRegister answering badly rather than being absent, and each logs at warning naming what could not be read: the relation rows behind the Related cases tab, and the parentCase inheritance declaration. The third is a read miss on the parent of a sub-case. None is a refusal: every rule this change enforces is a guard in DeelzaakService or CaseRelationService that answers a reason the controller translates, which is why the duplicate, the self-relation, the hierarchy overlap and the case-type refusal are nowhere on this list. Merging development took the ceiling to 222 first, so it went 222 to 225 for those three and nothing else.

2026-09-15, openspec/changes/markers-and-assessments-on-the-case: ONE site arrived with CaseAttentionConditionService::contextFor, the read of the advice requests a marker condition asks about. It is a degradation of a read that may be unavailable, it logs at warning naming the case, and the empty value is load-bearing rather than tolerated: an empty CONTEXT means "not asked" and leaves every marker standing, where an empty ROW SET would mean "asked, and there is nothing" and would clear one. Collapsing the two would report a handler's work as done on no evidence, on every unrelated save. The ceiling went 225 to 226 for that one site and nothing else.

2026-09-15, openspec/changes/starter-content-and-templates: four sites arrived with the starter-content services. Three are StarterStore, the one OpenRegister seam nine services in that change read and write through, and the fourth is the mail half of the template library. The null there is load-bearing rather than tolerated: every caller reads null as "could not look" and the empty value as "looked, found none", and collapsing the two is how an undo strips access nobody checked for and how the shipped-configuration screen reports "nothing shipped" on an instance that could not read. Nothing on this list is a refusal: the refusals in that change are named reasons on the result (`not_found`, `changed_locally`, `role_in_use`, `in_use`) that the controllers translate to 404 and 409. The ceiling went 226 to 230 for those four and nothing else.

2026-09-15, openspec/changes/gemachtigde-role-on-every-case-type: two sites arrived with PartyIndicatorReader, the one place dossiq asks OpenRegister what a party's indicators refuse. Both are degradations of an OpenRegister that is absent or predates openregister#3761, and each logs at warning naming the read it could not make. The empty answer is deliberately fail-open: the same two refusals are enforced inside OpenRegister at the publication and at the send, so this reader is the sentence a handler sees rather than the only thing standing in the way, and refusing every publication on an instance with no party model would stop work that was never refused. The ceiling went 230 to 232 for those two and nothing else.

2026-09-16, openspec/changes/case-sharing-mints-access-links: four sites arrived with the case access links and two left. All four are degradations of an OpenRegister that may be absent or may predate openregister#3817, and each logs naming what it could not do. Two entries were removed rather than moved: `ConsultationRepository::findBySecureToken` and `OpenRegisterSharingGateway::caseTokenService` went with the token surface this change deleted, which nothing could enter because nothing minted its token. None of the four is a refusal, and one candidate was converted rather than listed: reading the comments on a case now throws when the read cannot be made, because answering "nothing new" would tell a handler the advisory body had not replied when its advice was sitting there unread. The ceiling went 233 to 235 for those four and nothing else.

2026-09-17, openspec/changes/duplicate-warning-at-intake: ONE site arrived with DuplicatePolicy::askDetection, the one place dossiq asks OpenRegister's duplicate scorer anything. It is a degradation of an OpenRegister that is absent or answers badly, and it logs at warning naming the question it could not ask. The first draft had three sites for this one degradation, a container resolver and one catch per question; they were collapsed into one before landing rather than listed. Nothing on this list is a refusal: a case type that blocks a duplicate throws RefusedException, which IntakeRequirementsListener turns into the refused save. The ceiling went 235 to 236 for that one site and nothing else.

2026-09-18, openspec/changes/decision-outcomes-on-the-case: two sites arrived with the approval gate and the admissibility verdict. Both turn an unreadable case type into a REFUSAL rather than a write, and each logs at warning naming the case type. Neither is a fail-open: the gate answers 503 and the verdict is refused as undeclared. A third candidate was converted rather than listed, CaseRemedy::caseTypeOf, which throws, because a besluit printed with no bezwaarclausule on the strength of a failed read is a decision somebody cannot object to in time.

2026-09-18, the parity/round2 quality sweep: eighteen sites arrived with the case merge, the split and its incidents, the custody chain and its takeover, the consent gate, pipelinq's party-kind acceptance and the working-day roll. Eleven are degradations of OpenRegister, pipelinq or the organisation calendar being absent or answering badly, and each logs at warning naming what it could not read; seven are read misses on a stored value, five of them a date the reader reports as undated rather than inventing a moment. None is a refusal: every rule these changes enforce throws RefusedException and is translated by its controller, which is why the merge's, the split's and the hand-off's own refusals are nowhere on this list. The ceiling went 238 to 269, and only eighteen of those thirty-one are this entry's: the file already held 251 entries against a ceiling of 238, because thirteen earlier changes on this branch added their sites and left the number alone. That is why the ceiling assertion was red before any of the eighteen were written, and it is the reason the number is restated here rather than incremented.

classes.refusal: A rule said no. Throw a typed exception and let the controller translate it (ADR-105). Never allowlisted: converting it is the fix.
classes.degradation: A sibling app, an engine or a container binding is absent. Keep the catch, log at warning naming what was absent, return the documented empty value.
classes.read-miss: An object was not found on a read. Answering null is right; the catch is how the store reports the miss.

sites.reason: `provenanceForCase()` answers `return null` when OpenRegister's evaluator throws; the catch logs at warning naming the case ("OpenRegister could not answer the provenance for a case") and the caller publishes the action list exactly as it would without OpenRegister. Null is deliberately NOT false here: reading "we could not ask" as "refused" would empty every case's action list on every instance that has not upgraded to openregister#3726.

The empty context is deliberately NOT an empty row set: an empty row set means "asked, and there is nothing outstanding" and CLEARS the marker, so reading a store that was briefly unreachable as an answer would report a handler's work as done on no evidence at all, on every unrelated save of the case, and nothing anywhere would fail. Raising is not open either: this runs inside a pre-persist listener, so a throw would fail the user's save over a marker.

The null is LOAD-BEARING rather than tolerated, and it is the distinction the whole change turns on: every caller reads null as "could not look" and `[]` as "looked, found none". Collapsing the two is how an undo strips access nobody checked for (MunicipalRoleSetService::rolesHoldingGrants treats null as in-use), and how a shipped-configuration screen reads "nothing shipped" on an instance whose schema key was never written. tests/Unit/Service/MunicipalRoleSetTest.php::testAnUnreadableGrantStoreStopsTheUndo pins it.

`save()` answers `return null` when the write cannot be made; the catch logs at ERROR, not warning, naming the schema and the id, because a failed write is not a degraded read. Every caller checks it and reports: the domain copy adds the row to `notCarried` and answers 207 rather than a green tick, and the adoption answers `write_failed`. Nothing here treats a failed write as a success.

The write half of the same seam. Null is the documented 'not persisted', and the caller surfaces it rather than reporting a plan it did not store.

`countIn()` counts the cases in a status, to decide whether the status is at capacity. Null is NOT zero here and the caller knows it: zero would read as 'the status is free' and let a transition through, so null means 'not counted' and the guard abstains. The comment above the query records the openregister#3611 filter trap this method survives.

Null means the calendar did not answer, and the caller then starts the term on the moment it already had rather than guessing a working day; a silent fallback to 'today is a working day' would start a citizen's clock on a Sunday on any instance without OpenRegister. `rows()` answers `return []` when OpenRegister cannot be searched for the incidents on a case; the catch logs at warning naming the read. The empty list is "could not look", and the incidents tab draws nothing rather than claiming a case has no reports.

`holdings()` answers `return []` when OpenRegister cannot be searched for the custody chain of a case; the catch logs at warning naming the case. The chain is only meaningful whole, so an unreadable one draws nothing rather than a chain with a gap in it that reads like a case nobody held.

`heldBy()` answers `return []` when OpenRegister cannot be searched for what a unit holds; the catch logs at warning naming the unit. The empty list is "could not look", and the caller reports no holdings rather than reporting that a unit holds nothing.
`instant()` answers `return null` for a stored custody moment that cannot be read, so a holding with an unreadable date is reported undated rather than placed in the chain at a moment nobody wrote.

`rows()` answers `return []` when OpenRegister cannot be searched for the takeover requests on a case; the catch logs at warning. The empty list is "could not look": a handler sees no request rather than being told nobody has asked for the case.

`instant()` answers `return null` for a stored takeover moment that cannot be read. The escalation clock then treats the request as undated rather than as raised at a moment nobody wrote, which is what would make it escalate on invented evidence.

`consentsFor()` answers `return []` when OpenRegister cannot be searched for the consents recorded on a case; the catch logs at warning naming the case. The empty list does NOT open the gate: `assess()` reads no consent as no consent, so a hand-off across an organisation boundary is refused rather than allowed on a read that failed.

`instant()` answers `return null` for a stored consent moment that cannot be read. A consent whose `until` cannot be read is treated as carrying no expiry the gate can verify, which narrows rather than widens what it allows.

`objectService()` answers `return null` when OpenRegister's object service cannot be resolved. Null is the documented "this instance has no store to declare into", and `declareAcceptance()` reports pipelinq's own fallback rather than writing an acceptance nobody can read back.

`existingAcceptanceId()` answers `return null` when the existing acceptance row cannot be looked up. Null means "could not look", and the caller then writes a new row rather than overwriting one it cannot see; a duplicate acceptance is recoverable, a silent overwrite of another app's row is not.

`endAfter()` answers `return null` when the organisation calendar refuses a working-day end date; the catch logs at warning. Null is deliberately NOT a date: `TermijnService::endDateFor()` reads it as "the calendar did not answer", logs that the term is SHORTER than it is owed, and counts calendar days, which is the documented D-2 degradation.

`daysBetween()` answers `return null` when the organisation calendar refuses a working-day span; the catch logs at warning. Null means "the calendar did not answer", and the caller falls back to calendar days rather than reporting a span computed on a calendar nobody administered.
